speaker: Rafael Montez
cascadeSummary: OPD will implement targeted patrol adjustments in East and West Oakland based on CrimeIndex data, focusing on high-frequency incident areas while maintaining citywide response capacity. The department continues to refine OARI co-deployment protocols in pilot districts.

statements.decision: Redeploy 4 additional marked units to East Oakland and 3 to West Oakland based on CrimeIndex data
statements.quote: Public safety resources must follow the data — that's why we're adjusting patrol deployments to match incident frequency in our highest-need neighborhoods.
statements.fullStatement: Chief Rafael Montez announced operational adjustments to address elevated CrimeIndex figures in East Oakland (1.20) and West Oakland (1.19). Effective immediately, OPD will redeploy 4 additional marked units to East Oakland and 3 to West Oakland, prioritizing areas with highest incident frequency. These deployments will operate alongside existing neighborhood safety initiatives and OARI co-response operations. The department maintains citywide response capacity through real-time dispatch coordination. Crime trends will be reassessed after 30 days of enhanced patrol presence.

statements.decision: Continue current OARI co-deployment protocols in pilot districts
statements.quote: Behavioral health crisis response requires careful operational integration — we're methodically refining the co-deployment model district by district.
statements.fullStatement: The Oakland Police Department continues to work with OARI program leadership to refine crisis response protocols in pilot districts (D1, D3, D5). Current co-deployment procedures remain in effect while performance data is analyzed. Chief Montez emphasized that public safety integration of alternative responders requires measured operational planning: 'We're assessing response times, scene outcomes, and officer safety metrics before considering expansion.' The next quarterly evaluation of OARI-OPD coordination will occur in Cycle 105.
